

Process emissions are by-products released during chemical reactions and physical transformations of materials, that are not accounted for elsewhere in your PCF.

This does not apply to all manufacturing processes. To learn more about process emissions, a range of sector-specific guides are available from: The GHG Protocol

Process emissions include by-product emissions from the chemical and physical transformation of raw materials.


Typical examples include

• Emissions from the calcination step in cement

  manufacture,

• PFC emissions from aluminium smelting

• N2O emissions from catalytic cracking.

Application of plant protection product, by field sprayer

1 m2 | This dataset represents the application of protection product in one hectare (ha). In this operation occurs the application of herbicides, fungicides and insecticides. Functional Unit (FU) is one hectare of application of plant protection product. The operation time is about 0.11 hours per ha. However, only 62.5% of this time is spent performing the operation, the remaining fraction is time for maintenance, waiting in the field and re-allocations between the field plots.

EN16258

ICAO/IATA RP 1678

Account for the transportation of this material from your direct supplier to you. Please include for all segments of this journey.

Save

Cancel



Transport profiles should account for the entire journey a material takes from your direct supplier to your facility.


To do that:

1. Set up the material’s journey by adding transport

    segments, and select the mode of transport used in each

    segment of the journey.

2. Record the distance traveled in each segment of the journey.


The profile will then be ready for this material for use in all PCF calculations.
